title: South Korea: Seoul Food and Shopping

cover.alt: An adult traveller chooses Korean market food, with a palace gate and Seoul shopping street beyond.

blocks.title: Seoul: Food, History, and Shopping
paragraphs: Seoul is the capital of South Korea, a country in East Asia. You will read about a historic food market, a royal palace, and a busy shopping street. Then you will practise three real conversations: ordering food, asking about the subway, and choosing a jacket size.

items.prompt: Have you ever visited a food market or a shopping street in a big city? What did you see or buy?
items.explanation: There is no single correct answer. Think about any market or busy shopping area you know.

items.prompt: What do you know about South Korea or Seoul already?
items.explanation: Any answer is fine. You might think of food, music, or sport.

blocks.title: Gwangjang Market and Korean Food
paragraphs: Gwangjang Market is a historic market in Seoul. It has food stalls and shops for clothing and fabric. Two foods to try are mayak gimbap and nokdujeon. Mayak gimbap are small rice rolls, and nokdujeon are savoury pancakes made from mung beans. Another important Korean food is kimchi. Families and communities make and share kimchi in a tradition called kimjang. UNESCO added kimjang to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2013.

items.answer: Savoury pancakes made from mung beans
items.explanation:
Nokdujeon are savoury pancakes made from mung beans, a popular street food at Gwangjang Market.

Would you like to try mayak gimbap or nokdujeon? Why?

rows.meaning: Ask for food or a drink politely.
rows.example: Can I have this, please? — pointing at the gimbap

rows.meaning: Ask for one item when you point.
rows.example: One of these, please.

rows.meaning: Add a request for water.
rows.example: Can I have this and some water, please?

rows.meaning: Ask for the price.
rows.example: How much is it?

rows.meaning: A warm way to say thank you.
rows.example: Thank you so much!

blocks.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Subway
paragraphs: Gyeongbokgung was the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty. It was established in 1395. Its name expresses a wish for the new dynasty to enjoy great fortune and prosperity. Important cultural work took place there, including work connected to Hunminjeongeum, the original name of the Korean alphabet. The palace was destroyed in 1592 and restored in 1867. If you travel there, check a current subway map and ask for help when you need it.

items.explanation:
Gyeongbokgung was established in 1395 as the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty.

Would you like to visit Gyeongbokgung? What would you most want to learn there?

rows.meaning: Ask which subway line to take.
rows.example: Which line goes to Gyeongbokgung?

rows.term: Can you show me on the map?
rows.meaning: Ask someone to point to the route on a current map.
rows.example: Can you show me on the map, please?

rows.meaning: Check that you are waiting in the correct place.
rows.example: Is this the right platform?

rows.term: Do I need to change trains?
rows.meaning: Ask if you need to move to another train.
rows.example: Do I need to change trains?

rows.meaning: Thank someone politely for directions.
rows.example: Thank you, that's very helpful!

blocks.title: Myeong-dong Shopping
paragraphs: Myeong-dong is a shopping area in central Seoul. It is known for fashion and food. The area also has Myeong-dong Cathedral and two major department stores. You can visit shops, compare clothes, and stop for something to eat. When you buy clothes, check the label because size systems can be different. If you are not sure, ask, ‘What size is this?’ or ‘Can I try this on?’

items.prompt: What is a good idea when you buy clothes while travelling?
items.answer: Check the label and try the item on
items.explanation:
Size systems can be different, so checking the label and trying the item on can help you choose.

Have you ever had trouble finding the right clothing size when travelling? What did you do?

rows.term: Do you have this in a bigger size?
rows.meaning: Ask for a larger size of the same item.
rows.example: Do you have this jacket in a bigger size?

rows.meaning: Ask to try on a piece of clothing.
rows.example: Can I try this on, please?

rows.meaning: Ask where to try clothes.
rows.example: Where is the fitting room?

rows.term: This is too small / too big.
rows.meaning: Describe how the clothing fits.
rows.example: This is too small. Do you have another size?

rows.meaning: Ask about the size on a clothing label.
rows.example: What size is this jacket?

blocks.title: Situation: At Gwangjang Market
paragraphs: You are at Bakgane Bindaetteok in Gwangjang Market. A menu card lists one mung bean pancake for 5,000 won. The vendor smiles and waits for your order.
Your goal is to order one pancake, ask for water, and confirm the price.

images.alt: A vendor serves mayak gimbap and golden nokdujeon to a traveller at a covered Seoul market.

turns.speaker: Vendor
turns.text: Hello! What would you like?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can I have one mung bean pancake, please?

turns.speaker: Vendor
turns.text: Of course. One bindaetteok. Anything else?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: And some water, please.

turns.speaker: Vendor
turns.text: Sure. Here you are.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: How much is the pancake?

turns.speaker: Vendor
turns.text: It is 5,000 won, as shown on the menu.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Here is 5,000 won. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Vendor
turns.text: Thank you. Enjoy your food!

blocks.title: Situation: At the Subway Station
paragraphs: You are at Anguk Station in Seoul. You want to travel one stop to Gyeongbokgung Station for Gyeongbokgung Palace. A station worker is near the Line 3 map.
Your goal is to find the train direction, confirm whether you need to change, and choose the palace exit.

images.alt: A traveller holding a paper map asks a Seoul subway worker for directions beside a route board.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me. Which train should I take to Gyeongbokgung?

turns.speaker: Worker
turns.text: Take Line 3 toward Daehwa.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Do I need to change trains?

turns.speaker: Worker
turns.text: No. Gyeongbokgung is the next stop.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Which exit should I use for the palace?

turns.speaker: Worker
turns.text: Use Exit 5. The palace is about a two-minute walk.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. Now I know where to go.

turns.speaker: Worker
turns.text: You're welcome. Have a good trip!

blocks.title: Situation: At a Myeong-dong Clothing Store
paragraphs: You are at the SPAO store in Myeong-dong. You find a hooded windbreaker you like, but its label says XL (105). A shop assistant is nearby.
Your goal is to understand the Korean size number and ask to try the jacket on.

images.alt: A traveller checks a jacket label while a shop assistant helps her find the right size.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me. What does 105 mean on this jacket?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: For this jacket, 105 is the XL size.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. Can I try it on?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Of course. Please come this way.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Great. Thank you for your help.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: You're welcome. I hope it fits well!

blocks.title: Your Turn: Talk About Seoul
blocks.intro: Use what you have read and practised. Try to speak for one minute on each question.

items.prompt: You are telling a friend about Seoul. Describe one place you want to visit and what you would do there.
items.explanation:
I want to visit ... because ...

Use words from the article: market, palace, shopping, subway, food stall, fitting room.

items.prompt: Imagine you are at Gwangjang Market. Your friend asks what to order. What do you say?
items.explanation:
You should try ... because ...

Think about the foods from the article: mayak gimbap, nokdujeon, kimchi.

items.prompt: Which of the three places in Seoul — Gwangjang Market, Gyeongbokgung Palace, or Myeong-dong — would you most like to visit? Why?
items.explanation: Any answer is good. Use details from the article to explain your choice.

items.prompt: Which conversation felt most useful for a real trip: ordering food, asking for subway directions, or checking a clothing size? Why?
items.explanation: Think about your own travel experiences or plans.

items.prompt: What is one new word or phrase from today that you want to remember?
items.explanation: Choose any word or phrase that felt new or useful to you.

rows.meaning: A place where people buy and sell food or goods.
rows.example: Gwangjang Market has food and clothing stalls.

rows.meaning: A large building where a royal family lived.
rows.example: Gyeongbokgung is a palace established in 1395.

rows.meaning: The area in a station where you wait for a train.
rows.example: Please check the correct platform before you board.

rows.meaning: A small piece of cloth or paper on an item that gives information such as its size.
rows.example: Check the label before you buy the jacket.

rows.meaning: A person who sells things, often at a stall or market.
rows.example: The vendor took our order.

rows.meaning: A small room in a shop where you can try on clothes.
rows.example: I tried the jacket on in the fitting room.

rows.meaning: Important traditions or buildings passed down through history.
rows.example: UNESCO recognised kimjang as cultural heritage in 2013.
